content: Cephradine is a first-generation cephalosporin antibiotic. It is chemically and pharmacologically similar to cefalexin and is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. Indications: 1. Respiratory Tract Infections: Cephradine is effective in treating respiratory tract infections such as tonsillitis, pharyngitis, and lobar pneumonia caused by Group A beta-hemolytic streptococci and Streptococcus pneumoniae (formerly known as Diplococcus pneumoniae). While penicillin remains the preferred treatment for streptococcal infections and the prevention of rheumatic fever, cephradine (marketed as Velosef) can effectively eradicate streptococci from the nasopharynx. However, there is currently insufficient evidence to confirm its efficacy in preventing rheumatic fever. 2. Otitis Media: Cephradine is used to treat middle ear infections caused by Group A beta-hemolytic streptococci, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and staphylococci. 3. Skin and Skin Structure Infections: This antibiotic is effective against skin infections caused by staphylococci (both penicillin-susceptible and penicillin-resistant strains) and beta-hemolytic streptococci. 4. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Cephradine is used to treat UTIs, including prostatitis, caused by Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella species, and enterococci (Enterococcus faecalis). The high concentrations of cephradine achieved in the urinary tract make it effective against many strains of enterococci, even those that may show relative resistance in disc susceptibility studies. However, it is important to note that among beta-lactam antibiotics, ampicillin is the preferred treatment for enterococcal urinary tract infections caused by E. faecalis. Formulations: Cephradine is available in the following forms: Capsules containing 250 mg or 500 mg of the drug. Syrup containing 250 mg per 5 mL. Injectable vials containing 500 mg or 1 g of the drug. Brand Names: Cephradine is marketed under various brand names internationally, including: Velocef and Infexin (by Merck Pvt. Ltd.) Intracef (by Beximco Pharma) Sefril (by The ACME Laboratories Ltd., Bangladesh) Reocef (by Rephco Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Bangladesh) Lebac (by Square Pharmaceuticals Ltd., Bangladesh).
